# Pointers

@difference Extension: the `Pointer` type, written `Name*` or `Name:Pointer`, holds the address of something in memory and is as wide as the platform's pointers.

The originals have no way to keep an address in a variable. BlitzLLVM has the `Pointer` type for it: 32 bits wide on x86 and 64 bits wide on x86_64 and arm64, so it always fits an address of the platform. It is written with a star behind the name (`address*`, the short notation, like `%`, `#` and `$`) or as `address:Pointer` (the long notation). Both work everywhere a type can be written: `Local`, `Global`, `Const`, parameters, function results, `Field`s, `Dim` arrays, and the parameters and results of functions in a [userlib](Userlib-Declarations).

```blitzbasic
Local address* = Null
Local other:Pointer = Pointer(4096)

Function Same*(value*)
	Return value
End Function

If address <> other Then Print Long(Same(other))
```

* A Pointer starts as `Null`, and `Null` is the only Pointer that a program can write down. Everything else comes from a function of a userlib that returns one, or from [Pointer](Pointer) with a whole number.
* A Pointer can be compared with a Pointer or `Null` with `=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=`. The addresses are compared without a sign. In `If`, `While` and `Until` a Pointer is true when it is not `Null`. A Pointer is not compared with a whole number.
* A Pointer takes no part in calculations, and nothing is converted to or from a Pointer for you: `p = 5`, `p + 1` and `Local i = p` are errors. Use [Pointer](Pointer) for a whole number, and `Int`, `Long`, `ULong` or the other conversions of [Numbers of other sizes](Numbers-of-Other-Sizes) to get the address as a number (`Long(p) + 8` is a calculation, `Pointer(Long(p) + 8)` goes back). `Int(p)` loses the upper half of a 64-bit address, `Long` and `ULong` do not. `Str(p)` is the same as `Str(ULong(p))`.
* `Int(object)` still gives the handle of an object and not its address. A Pointer to an object is not available yet.
* In a userlib, `*` and `:Pointer` can now be used for the result of a function too. As a parameter a Pointer is passed as it is, while a whole number is still taken as a bank and passed as the address of the bank's memory.

### The star is not always a Pointer

`a*b` is a multiplication, and the star of a Pointer name is only a part of the name where nothing can be multiplied or where nothing follows it: in the declaration of a variable, a parameter, a field, an array or a function (`Local p*`, `Function F*(a*)`), and anywhere else when the next thing is not the start of an operand. `p* = q`, `If p* = Null`, and a `p*` at the end of a line are Pointers, while `a*b`, `a*(b)`, `a*-b` and `a * b` are multiplications. The star behind a name that is followed by an operand is a multiplication even when the name was declared as a Pointer, so leave the star off after the declaration (the type is known by then, like with `%`, `#` and `$`), or use `p:Pointer`.
